method: Publisher CLI (python -m publisher publish --wait) against the public API as one throwaway test account, 20 s 640x360 H.264/AAC clips, one publisher process and cookie jar per clip so uploads run concurrently (a shared cookie jar serialises publishers on its lock file). Encoder tasks counted from ECS list-tasks every 5 s and from each task's createdAt/startedAt/stoppedAt. Work-queue sends from CloudWatch AWS/SQS (1 minute resolution). Nothing here is a Lambda-internal timestamp: queue wait is derived from job status transitions and ECS stamps, not from the Processing database.

launcher_config_observed.worker_task_definition: dc2-live-worker:1 (before the Processing release adopted a newer one)

single_job_cold.note: first job after the CD smoke; Aurora and the launcher were idle
single_job_cold.includes: upload, finalize, Aurora resume, Media to Processing command, Processing dispatch, launcher start-on-enqueue

encoder_task_timing_n12.note: 12 tasks of the first four runs (single jobs and the 3-way run)
encoder_task_timing_n12.interpretation: Fargate cold start is about 25 s of every encoder's life; the issue's 20 s warm single-job queue-wait target cannot be met by a task that starts on enqueue, only by a warm pool. The launcher itself is invoked within about 1 s of the work send (invocations at :02 or :13 past the minute, off the one-minute rule's tick).

three_clips_concurrent.result: PASS for 0 -> 3 -> 0; the queue-wait target of 20 s is NOT met (about 37 s observed queued-to-processing, 25 s of it Fargate start)

serialised_runs_with_shared_cookie_jar.note: Two earlier 3-clip runs shared one cookie jar, so the Publisher processes ran one after another (one encoder at a time, a work message every 2 minutes). They measured the client, not the platform, and are not used for scaling numbers.

backlog_nine_clips.calculated_serial_baseline_basis: 9 jobs x (25.6 s start + 33.1 s run), one encoder at a time, no queueing overhead; a calculation, not a measured single-encoder run
backlog_nine_clips.caveat: The launcher cap is fixed at 3 on this environment, so cap 1 and cap 2 were not run. This is not the 1/2/3-worker comparison of r1018b (which is a separate FAIL at 1.449x for 2 workers). Nine clips is a small sample, one run.
backlog_nine_clips.side_effect: CloudWatch counted 21 sends to ProcessingWork for 9 jobs. After the run 10 messages stayed visible in the queue with every job done and no encoder started for them, until the queue was purged by hand. The next CD smoke refused to run because of them (see README findings).
